articles.title: Jennifer Aniston’s Boyfriend Makes Rare, Candid Comments About Their Relationship
articles.excerpt: Jennifer Aniston’s boyfriend, Jim Curtis, is opening up about their relationship, and his sweet comments about the 'Friends' star have us swooning. Here’s what he had to say.
articles.content:
With the rom-com renaissance in full swing and buzzy dramas like Heated Rivalry, The Summer I Turned Pretty and Sterling Point keeping us fully invested, it’s easy to understand why we’re all in our swooning era. But Jennifer Aniston’s boyfriend, Jim Curtis, just gave us a reason to swoon over a real-life romance, too.

Curtis, 50, appeared on the August 31 episode of The Jamie Kern Lima Show, where he opened up about his relationship with the Friends star, 57, and shared that "it's going really well."

As for what it’s like being with Aniston? Curtis had nothing but sweet things to say.

“My experience of her is so grounded and so open and caring and kind and loving,” Curtis said. “I feel blessed to be in a relationship with someone that is so open-hearted and kind and loving.”

Curtis, a hypnotherapist, also praised the people in Aniston’s inner circle, calling them “such a beautiful community and group of people.”

“I feel incredibly blessed to be part [of] and welcomed into that family,” he said.

And apparently, the warm welcome is just one part of what makes Aniston’s circle so special.

“It really speaks to her — and them — that everybody is so grounded, so kind. And it’s not just to me,” he said. “There’s a reason why that whole group and community is so beloved.”

Aniston and Curtis have been together for more than a year now. Romance rumors first started swirling in summer 2025, when the actress began soft-launching her new relationship. By September 2025, the pair had made things Instagram official, with Aniston sharing a heartfelt birthday tribute to her "love."

Alongside a black-and-white photo of the couple embracing, with Aniston’s arms wrapped around Curtis from behind, she wrote, “Happy birthday my love [red heart emoji] Cherished.”

articles.title: Kalshi bans ex-congressman George Santos for life after suspicious trades
articles.excerpt: George Santos faces a lifetime ban from Kalshi after failing to cooperate with the prediction market's investigation into his alleged unlawful trades.
articles.content:
Updated on: August 31, 2026 / 11:11 AM EDT / CBS News

Kalshi has permanently banned George Santos from its prediction market platform after the former New York lawmaker failed to cooperate with the company's investigation into allegedly unlawful trades he made related to his attendance at the 2026 State of the Union address.

A Kalshi spokesperson said Santos is being banned due to "his lack of cooperation" with its compliance department, which was investigating trades the company said netted him nearly $18,000 in profits. The prediction market also penalized him $71,356, a filing on the company's website shows.

Santos represented New York's 3rd District in the House of Representatives before he was expelled in 2023 after being charged with fraud and campaign finance violations.

In July, Santos agreed to pay $35,000 to settle a federal probe into his suspicious trades on Kalshi. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission also imposed a three-year trading ban on Santos.

articles.title: Verdict watch continues in Lindsay Clancy trial: LIVE UPDATES
articles.excerpt: Jurors in the Lindsay Clancy trial continue to deliberate. Watch a live stream and get live updates on the verdict watch.
articles.content:
Over the past five weeks, the jury heard testimony from doctors, first responders, relatives and even Clancy’s former husband.

Jurors in the closely watched Lindsay Clancy trial began deliberating last week, but had not reached a verdict by the end of the day Friday. They resumed their deliberations shortly after 9 a.m. ET Monday.

They have a lot to consider.

Stream NBC10 Boston news for free, 24/7, wherever you are.

Over the past five weeks, the jury heard testimony from doctors, first responders, relatives and even Clancy’s former husband. It now weighs the question of whether she should be held criminally responsible for killing her three young children at her Massachusetts home in 2023.

Both sides agree Clancy did it. But her attorneys argue the former labor and delivery nurse was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time, and that poor mental healthcare exacerbated her condition. Prosecutors argue she intentionally planned the killings.

If Clancy is convicted, her sentence could be as severe as life in prison. If she’s found not guilty, she may be released or remain confined in a mental health facility.

As the jury continues deliberating, here are moments from the trial they may be considering.

Local

In-depth news coverage of the Greater Boston and New England area.

Postpartum expert talks Lindsay Clancy trial, impact of social media misinformation

Firefighters battling large fire in multi-family home in Brighton

Clancy’s former husband made anguished 911 call

Clancy’s former husband, Patrick Clancy, was first to take the stand.

In emotional testimony, he described the day he found his wife after she tried to kill herself.

Lindsay Clancy had sent him out to get takeout food and medication for their daughter, which prosecutors argue was an excuse to get him out of the house.

He came home to find the house unusually silent, before finding blood throughout the main bedroom and a window open.

Jurors listened to the 911 call Patrick Clancy made after finding his wife outside in the snow. Clancy can be heard speaking with his wife, then tells the dispatcher he’s going to check on the children.

Moments later, he howls and cries after finding his children in the basement. The confused dispatcher repeatedly asks what happened.

“She killed the kids!” he yells.

Everyone knew Clancy was struggling

Clancy’s mother, mother-in-law, sister, friends and co-workers testified that Clancy struggled with her mental health after giving birth to Callan, the youngest of her three children.

Clancy’s mother-in-law, Susan Clancy, said she and her former daughter-in-law were close. Both worked as labor and delivery nurses. She described Lindsay as a wonderful mother.

But Susan Clancy testified that Lindsay had become anxious, paranoid and suicidal, and that the psychiatric care she was getting wasn’t helping.

“She felt unwell. She had insomnia. She was losing her appetite. She was very anxious and sad,” Susan Clancy said. “She was begging for help.”

Lindsay Clancy’s mother, Paula Musgrove, testified that her daughter was scared of sleeping alone, became paranoid and believed the medications she was taking “were destroying her mind.”

“Mom, will you please come up and stay with me for a bit? I’m really sick. Something is wrong,” Clancy wrote in an October 2022 text message that Paula Musgrove read in court. “I had horrible insomnia all night, and I just don’t know how I am going to get through the day. … It’s just really scary, and I don’t want to be alone.”

The defense questioned the quality of Clancy’s medical care

Clancy saw several doctors about her declining mental health, and eventually checked herself in to a psychiatric hospital.

Her lawyer, Kevin Reddington, argued that she was misdiagnosed and overmedicated.

As he cross-examined one of her psychiatrists, Dr. Jennifer Tufts, Reddington questioned her expertise, prescribing decisions and use of 25-minute video appointments with limited time for talk therapy.

At one point, Reddington implied that Tufts was a box-checking “robot.”

“What did you do? You had a woman who was telling you she felt hopeless,” he asked as they discussed an appointment about two months before the killings.

“I told her that this was something we could address, that there was hope, that there are treatments, that there are different types of programs,” Tufts said, “so she knew that she still had options and a reason to hope.”

Clancy said she heard a voice telling her to kill

Paul Zeizel, a clinical and forensic psychologist who visited Lindsay Clancy in the hospital after she killed the children, testified that he overheard her saying that a disembodied male voice had told her she had no choice but to kill her children and then herself. Zeizel said he believed Clancy wasn’t responsible for her actions because of her deep mental illness.

Prosecutors called a rebuttal witness, forensic psychologist Kirk Heilbrun, who said he didn’t believe Clancy had hallucinated voices.

“One of the things that she said when I asked about what happened, is that in the course of strangling each child, she said, ‘Go to God, baby. Go to God,’” he said. “That was part of her expectation that she and the children would be together in heaven with God.”

Dr. Gregory Saathoff, a senior psychiatrist for the FBI’s Behavioral Analysis Unit, testified for prosecutors that Clancy “had the capacity to know right from wrong.”

The lawyers got the last word

After testimony was complete, each side got about an hour to make their closing argument to the jury.

Reddington showed the jury a photograph of the Clancy family, looking happy, and a second one of Lindsay Clancy in the hospital.

“How does this turn into this?” Reddington asked. “How? Because of the damn medicine and the lousy medical care that she got.”

Prosecutor Jennifer Sprague said criticizing the mental health system was “a distraction.” She said Clancy chose to kill her children because doing so would make it easier to kill herself.

“She was depressed. She was exhausted. She was done. She didn’t want to try anymore. She felt damaged,” Sprague said. “But those kids, those kids were her protective factor. Those kids were keeping her from ending her misery.”

Costco Wholesale remains in focus as membership strength, warehouse expansion, delivery upgrades and valuation pressure reshape the discussion around its next phase of growth.

Costco Wholesale (NASDAQ:COST) Consumer Defensive Costco Wholesale Corp (NASDAQ:COST) 945.47 USD +10.810 ↑ 1.157% Last Updated at: 2026-08-28T20:05:00Z has returned to the spotlight after its latest share-price weakness raised fresh questions about valuation, growth durability and operating execution. The company remains one of the most closely followed names in large-scale retail because its business combines recurring membership revenue, high customer loyalty and a broad warehouse network with a reputation for disciplined merchandising.

The recent decline does not change the fundamental structure of Costcos business, but it does shift attention toward whether the company can continue supporting a premium market valuation through steady operating progress. That makes membership trends, store expansion, digital convenience and margin discipline more important than short-term price movement alone.

Costco also remains a significant name within the broader Nasdaq Composite, where large consumer-focused companies can react sharply when expectations around growth or valuation begin to change.

Membership Engine Stays Central

Costcos membership model remains one of its most distinctive strengths. Customers pay recurring fees for access to warehouses, creating a predictable revenue stream that supports the companys broader retail economics.

The importance of membership extends beyond fee income. Loyal members tend to visit regularly, purchase across multiple categories and engage with additional services offered through the Costco ecosystem. That gives the company an operating model that differs from many traditional retailers that depend more heavily on merchandise margins alone.

The next stage of Costcos growth story will depend partly on whether membership engagement remains strong as consumers become more selective with spending. Renewal behaviour, new sign-ups and member activity will remain useful indicators of business quality.

Warehouse Expansion Adds Scale

Physical expansion continues to be another major part of Costcos strategy. New warehouse openings can increase geographic reach while creating fresh opportunities to attract members and deepen customer relationships.

The latest expansion activity reinforces the companys long-term focus on scale. Each new warehouse creates potential for additional membership income, merchandise sales and local brand visibility.

However, expansion also requires disciplined capital deployment. New locations must generate enough traffic and membership participation to justify the upfront cost of construction, staffing and inventory.

For Costco, the effectiveness of expansion can therefore be measured through a combination of member growth, warehouse productivity and long-term cash generation rather than location count alone.

Delivery Strategy Builds Convenience

Retail competition increasingly depends on convenience as much as physical scale. Costco has been strengthening delivery capabilities as customers expect easier access to large-ticket and frequently purchased products.

Improved delivery options can help the company deepen digital engagement while complementing its warehouse model. The opportunity lies in providing convenience without weakening the economics that make the traditional membership format attractive.

Costcos scale gives it meaningful purchasing power and a broad customer base, but delivery economics can still be challenging. Logistics expenses, fulfilment costs and customer expectations must remain carefully balanced.

This creates an important operating test: whether digital convenience can enhance customer engagement while maintaining Costcos disciplined cost structure.

Retail Economics Need Discipline

Costco operates within the broader consumer stock category, but its economics differ from many peers because low merchandise margins are supported by recurring membership income.

That structure allows the company to maintain competitive pricing while generating additional profitability from memberships. It also means operating discipline remains essential.

Small shifts in merchandise costs, freight expenses or promotional activity can influence the relationship between sales growth and profitability. Costcos ability to preserve its value-oriented positioning while protecting cash economics remains a central part of the business case.

Valuation Raises Fresh Questions

Costco has historically attracted a premium valuation compared with many large retailers because the market places significant weight on its membership model, customer loyalty and earnings consistency.

That premium creates a higher operating bar. When a company trades at an elevated valuation, even modest changes in expectations can create a stronger share-price response.

The latest pullback therefore brings valuation back into focus. The key question is whether future business growth can remain strong enough to justify continued confidence in Costcos premium positioning.

Rather than focusing on a single trading session, the more useful approach is to examine whether revenue quality, membership performance and operating efficiency continue supporting the long-term narrative.

Legal Issues Add Complexity

Tariff-related refunds and associated litigation introduce another area requiring attention. Legal disputes can create uncertainty around costs, customer perception and future financial obligations.

For a company with Costcos scale, isolated legal matters may not redefine the entire business. However, they can still affect margins or operating flexibility depending on their scope and duration.

The important factor is whether such issues remain contained or develop into a more meaningful financial pressure.

Official filings and company disclosures will provide the clearest evidence of how these matters affect operating results.

Competition Remains Intense

Costco operates in a highly competitive retail environment where consumers can choose among warehouse clubs, discount retailers, online platforms and traditional department stores.

Its competitive advantage comes from combining membership economics with value-oriented merchandising and a strong customer reputation.

However, competition remains relevant because changing consumer preferences can influence store traffic and spending patterns. Retailers increasingly compete across price, convenience, digital services and product availability.

Costcos ability to defend customer loyalty while expanding services will remain one of the most important indicators of competitive strength.

Cash Conversion Matters Most

The strongest evidence for Costcos long-term performance will come from how effectively reported growth converts into cash generation.

Warehouse expansion, delivery improvements and membership growth all require resources. The company therefore needs to maintain a balance between reinvestment and operating efficiency.

Healthy cash generation can provide flexibility to support future store openings, technology improvements and shareholder distributions without creating unnecessary balance-sheet pressure.

That makes cash conversion a useful measure when evaluating whether growth remains economically attractive.

What Comes Next

Costcos next phase will likely be judged through membership trends, warehouse productivity, digital expansion and margin discipline.

The market will also continue watching whether legal or tariff-related matters create meaningful cost pressure. At the same time, competitive intensity across retail remains a constant factor.

For now, Costcos story is less about a single share-price move and more about whether its established business model can continue producing reliable growth while supporting a demanding valuation.

The company still benefits from strong brand recognition, recurring membership income and a growing physical footprint. The next updates will show whether those advantages remain powerful enough to offset higher expectations and a changing retail environment.

articles.excerpt: Bradley Barcola joins Liverpool for a fee potentially rising to £123m; France winger becomes clubs second most expensive purchase behind £125m deal for Alexander Isak from Newcastle in 2025; Barcola follows Victor Munoz
articles.content:
Bradley Barcola joins Liverpool for a fee potentially rising to £123m; France winger becomes club's second most expensive purchase behind £125m deal for Alexander Isak from Newcastle in 2025; Barcola follows Victor Munoz and Ronald Araujo into Anfield this summer

Monday 31 August 2026 14:18, UK

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Liverpool have completed the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain.

Barcola has agreed a five-year contract at Anfield. Liverpool will pay a guaranteed £106m for the winger, with add-ons potentially taking the fee to £123m.

"It's a great pride to be able to play for Liverpool. I'm very happy," the 23-year-old told Liverpoolfc.com.

"It took a long time but I'm really happy today to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play.

  • Transfer Centre LIVE! | Liverpool news & transfers🔴
  • Liverpool fixtures & scores | FREE Liverpool highlights▶️
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺

"I hope to achieve very big things. First of all, winning the Premier League - it's one of my biggest dreams in my life. It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term - that's why I signed a long contract - and I hope I can do it."

There had been a gap in valuation between the two clubs earlier in the summer, with PSG previously asking for around £145m for the France international, but Barcola has now become Andoni Iraola's third major signing of the summer after Victor Munoz and Ronald Araujo, with Jeremy Jacquet also arriving having been signed in January.

Barcola becomes Liverpool's second most expensive signing of all time, following the £125m deal for Alexander Isak from Newcastle last summer. He has been a long-term target and only wanted to move to Anfield.

In signing both Barcola and Munoz, Liverpool feel they have achieved their objective for the window of reinforcing in wide areas. They are unlikely to make any late additions unless there are outgoings.

Manchester City have been in contact with Liverpool over a move for Cody Gakpo.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Is Barcola really the right winger to replace Salah?

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Callum Bishop:

Liverpool appear to have made their decision that Bradley Barcola is their Mohamed Salah replacement. Even if they don't naturally play on the same flank, Barcola will surely be looked at as the man to bring Salah's level of productivity from wide areas.

When you think of Salah in his pomp, you think of the goals he brought to the team by cutting in from the right flank. Perhaps there's an expectation for the Frenchman to provide similar returns. But is that really what Liverpool need from their wingers?

Salah had his least productive season at Anfield last campaign. There are a number of factors behind why that is, but one of those was a change in his role thanks to the introduction of two number nines.

When the middle man in the Liverpool attack was Roberto Firmino, it allowed Salah to be the person chances were created for as the Brazilian was far from a stereotypical goalscorer. However, when Hugo Ekitike and Alexander Isak arrived on Merseyside, Salah's modus operandi shifted. More of a provider, less of a finisher.

His record of 10 assists wasn't terrible, but what's interesting is that he only provided one for Ekitike and none for Isak.

Barcola is an incredibly talented player with major upside, but Ekitike and Isak may see his arrival as more of a hindrance in their desire to shine.

One thing is for sure. Jamie Carragher isn't convinced that the France international is the answer Liverpool need.

"He's a left winger for me," Carragher said. "They don't have anyone who looks comfortable playing on the right but they have four players in the squad before Barcola joins who can play off the left.

"In terms of balance of the squad, it's not the position Liverpool need."

articles.title: Lotus Is Bringing Back Combustion With A New Hybrid Supercar
articles.excerpt: Lotus Esprit Type 135 revives hybrid V8 and V6 power with sub-1.5-ton weight and 1,000-plus horsepower targets between Emira and Evija.
articles.content:
Lotus Type 135 Esprit targets a sub-1.5-ton curb weight and more than 1,000 hp as a bridge between Emira and Evija performance.

  • Lotus confirmed the Type 135, a mid-engine V8 hybrid due in 2028, will also get a V6 from Horse.
  • Lotus targets a sub-1.5-ton (3,307-pound) curb weight and more than 1,000 hp.
  • Lotus says Formula 1-derived motor tech reduces a typical 150 kW motor from 209 to about 44 pounds.

Lotus just told investors the Esprit is coming back with pistons, not just electrons. On an earnings call held August 27, CEO Feng Qingfeng confirmed the Type 135, a mid-engine hybrid V8 supercar due in 2028, and outlined plans for a possible V6 variant using hardware from Horse, the Geely-Renault joint venture already developing Lotus combustion components.

Autocar has also reported on the V6 joining the hybrid V8 in the new Esprit lineup. The pitch is simple: a supercar targeting around 1.5 tons with more than 1,000 horsepower on tap, sitting between the Emira sports car and the electric Evija hypercar. Lotus is calling it a bridge. It looks like a U-turn back to combustion, and a welcome one for anyone who feared Hethel had gone all-electric for good.

Lotus Theory 1 Concept

Hybrid V8 Confirmed, V6 Planned

Feng did not dodge how hard that weight target is. "Achieving that target with an 800V architecture, a hybrid system, a V8 engine and electric motor in [the car] just is not easy," he told analysts on the call. Lotus is leaning on Formula 1-derived motor tech to claw back the mass a hybrid system usually adds.

Earlier this year he described an F1-style electric motor concept for the Type 135 in a separate interview, comparing a typical 150-kilowatt unit that can weigh up to 209 pounds with a new design trimmed to about 44 pounds. That kind of diet turns the motor from a weight penalty into a key part of hitting the mass target.

Current plans call for power to route through a dual-clutch gearbox capable of handling serious torque without piling on pounds. Lotus has not yet fixed the gear count or confirmed the production plant for the Type 135. It is a far cry from the Esprit V8 restomod tribute cars that have circulated in recent years and marks a factory-built, clean-sheet return.

Performance Targets And Focus 2030 Context

Feng framed the car's job plainly. "The Type 135 will fill the gap between the Emira and Emeya, preserving the emotional connection Emira owners have with the Lotus mechanical handling, while leveraging V8 hybrid technology to approach the technical benchmark set by the Emeya."

On the same call, he said the car is expected to offer V6 and V8 variants, with the V8 version targeted to produce more than 1,000 horsepower while weighing around 1.5 tons. That expectation sits inside Lotus's wider Focus 2030 strategy, which formally commits the brand to a mix of combustion, plug-in hybrid and battery-electric models instead of an EV-only lineup.

Motor1's Take: It reconnects Hethel to combustion buyers while keeping Evija tech. How weight and complexity are balanced will shape whether this car reads as a natural Emira step or a costly halo model. Watch weight, price, and on-road handling when prototypes arrive. Those will tell if the bridge shortens the gap or simply creates one.

articles.title: Onslaught review – super soldier slasher doesn’t go hard enough
articles.excerpt: There’s a committed performance from a spunky Adria Arjona in the Guest director Adam Wingard’s decent B-movie but it’s missing some sharper weaponry
articles.content:
There’s a committed performance from a spunky Adria Arjona in the Guest director Adam Wingard’s decent B-movie but it’s missing some sharper weaponry

There’s something rather fascinating about an indie director who heads to the A-list before returning to their roots, a wider skillset and different perspective gained for better or worse. Working within a stricter system – the tiniest of choices being agreed upon by the largest of committees – can often be a creatively crushing experience that we’ve heard gruesomely detailed by many who survived it but the expansion of what one is allowed to technically do with a bigger budget can also be instructive and enriching. The dream scenario is bringing back the good and allowing the bad to inspire new work that makes the most of how unshackled one again now is.

There are plenty of examples of how this hasn’t worked. Neill Blomkamp following Elysium and Chappie with chintzy low-budget horror Demonic (easily his least effective film although since opening his own AI “studio” I imagine the worst is yet to come), Marc Forster following Quantum of Solace and World War Z with a blind Blake Lively film that, ironically, no one saw while Anna Boden and Ryan Fleck went from the greatness of Half Nelson to the blandness of Captain Marvel to the headache of Freaky Tales. But then we were also gifted with the hometown intimacy of Alfonso Cuarón’s Roma after he came back from space for Gravity and Hogwarts for the Prisoner of Azkaban while Karyn Kusama brushed off the nightmare of Æon Flux with the brilliantly creepy dinner party thriller The Invitation.

Adam Wingard is a writer-director who broke out with the original low-budget thrillers You’re Next and The Guest before moving on to franchise fare like 2016’s Blair Witch sequel, a Netflix adaptation of Death Note and then, with a combined budget of about $300m to play with, two Godzilla vs Kong films. He did an excellent job with the first and a so-so one with the second, perhaps reflecting his growing frustration with the limitations of wrangling franchise IP and after bowing out of more studio fare (he reportedly turned down Face/Off 2), he’s gone back to basics.

He calls his new film Onslaught “an A-plus B-movie” because he tried to deliver all of the gonzo fun of a B-movie but with the A polish he’s learned in recent years. I’d call it a B-minus success, Wingard certainly showcasing that polish (a movie that looks like an actual movie is something to be cherished in 2026) but not quite giving us enough of the raucous fun we were promised. There’s something strangely restrained and at times a little tame, as if he’s still haunted by the ghosts of Warner Bros execs peering over his shoulder and restraint isn’t really what you want in an action slasher about genetically engineered super soldiers …

The film imagines what would happen if an unstoppable Michael Myers or Jason Voorhees type was created and weaponised by the government (the first wink, wink scene has a line of Halloween pumpkins getting obliterated). Evil German doctor Hans Kammler (Wingard regular Dan Stevens, doing a lot and then some) calls them “the human equivalent of a heat-seeking missile” and after an experiment goes awry at a research facility, they are unleashed on the local population. Out in the desert, that number is rather small, mainly the unfortunate residents of a trailer park, managed by ex-soldier and single mother Celeste (Adria Arjona), battling PTSD while struggling to take care of a young daughter who’s more put together than she is.

With her in-trailer armoury of guns, it’s no surprise that Celeste is going to step up to the plate and it’s a deserved lead vehicle for Arjona, who has slowly become one of the more magnetic rising stars of late. She was easily the most attention-securing part of Zoe Kravitz’s patchy Epstein thriller Blink Twice, a film that acted as a perfect sizzle reel of both her action star and final girl capabilities and here she gets to shoot, quip and chainsaw her way to the centre of the frame (I look forward to seeing what she brings to Michael B Jordan’s Thomas Crown Affair remake next year yet the obligatory superhero role carries far less excitement). But as suited as Arjona is to the role, there’s a limit to what she’s able to do with it. The shallowness of her character isn’t a problem (there’s very little we needed to know about, say, Laurie Strode or Sarah Connor) but the situations she’s placed into are not quite thrilling or inventive enough.

In trying to tick off both action and slasher, Wingard often falls in the unsatisfying gap in-between. Arming slasher villains with guns is just plainly not that interesting (there’s a reason why Michael, Ghostface and Jason rarely touch them while even the killer in the 1981 second world war veteran horror The Prowler prefers a pitchfork) and even when they’re forced to improvise, there’s not enough gnarliness to the carnage. Wingard often decides to not even show it, as if he’s still trying to secure a studio-friendly PG-13 rating and it proves to be a strange mix of sanitised violence and brief flashes of gonzo perversity (Drew Starkey having plenty of fun as an S&M-loving cleanup agent having to hunt the soldiers down after having just taken MDMA or the perennially underused Rebecca Hall, a Wingard favourite, as a cold-hearted German dominatrix) and I wish Wingard had leaned harder on the latter, giving us the balls-to-the-wall mayhem we assumed we would be getting. For an action film it feels like we’re missing a set piece or two and for a slasher it feels like we’re missing some gore and seat-edge suspense. It’s decently entertaining and I appreciated Wingard transferring his sleek studio style but it just never goes hard enough. After all, we were promised an onslaught.

articles.title: ‘Onslaught’ Review: Adria Arjona Shines in Adam Wingard’s Intriguingly Colorful, Ultimately Underwhelming Action Thriller
articles.excerpt: Adria Arjona stars in 'Onslaught,' Adam Wingard's thriller also starring Dan Stevens and Drew Starkey, about an army vet attacked by super soldiers.
articles.content:
Dan Stevens, Drew Starkey and Rebecca Hall also star in the picture co-written by Simon Barrett, about an Army vet whose trailer park is attacked by a trio of experimental super soldiers.

If nothing else, Onslaught stands as proof that director Adam Wingard, making his way back to lean, mean originals after a decade in the IP mines, hasn’t lost his touch for the sort of deliciously vivid details that suggest motherlodes of stories unto themselves.

In the first few minutes alone, we get grinning jack-o’-lanterns lined up in a dusty canyon, exploding one by one in target practice. A knife slicing through gnarled, unpeeled carrots that look like nothing so much as human fingers. An ancient Nazi scientist (Dan Stevens) crawling across a carpet to lick a woman’s stilettoed foot.

Onslaught

Each image lands as a promise — an amuse-bouche for the veritable feast of ultraviolence sure to come once all these disparate elements start to crash and burn into one another. But building anticipatory buzz is one thing; paying it off is another. Gloriously crafted if narratively undercooked, the action-thriller is a pretty good time. It’s just that it had seemed for a moment like it was going to be a great one.

The pumpkin shooter turns out to be Celeste (Adria Arjona), a former Army sniper with the shaky hands, extensive gun collection and dirty-dish-filled sink of someone barely keeping it together. Wracked with PTSD, she’s retreated in her civilian life into a remote desert trailer park populated by other mild eccentrics who seem more comfortable removed from the rest of the world, including a kindly Vietnam vet (Reginald VelJohnson as Josiah) and a bitter drunk of a cop (Eric Wareheim as Kovacks).

But the relative safety of Windy Oasis is violated when a trio of super-soldiers escape from a top-secret military bunker up the road. As these experiments, described to one eager businessman as “the human equivalent of heat-seeking missiles,” close in, Celeste must take up arms to protect herself, her young daughter (Blake Kennedy’s Daisy) and her community.

In other words: Expect a home invasion thriller, of the sort Wingard made his name on in 2011’s You’re Next and 2014’s The Guest. On that front, Onslaught delivers well enough. Between the soldiers’ imperviousness to bullets, immunity to pain and indifference to conscience, it doesn’t take long before they rack up a body count in the dozens — chopping through walls and punching through windows and blowing off heads with cold, mechanical relentlessness.

Fine craftsmanship can be seen on every level of the action. Nick Interlandi’s soundscapes swell with the rat-a-tat of machine guns, or zero in on the precise, satisfying crunch of glass cracking under bone, while Oren Soffer’s cinematography runs the gamut from sickly clinical to startlingly sensual.

And yet, the second half of the movie can’t feel like something of a letdown — as if Wingard, having shown us all the cool shiny toys he has at his disposal, has forgotten to come up with anything to do with them beyond smash them together.

Stevens’ Kammler makes a big immediate impression as a pervy little freak, but then gets less room than you might hope to swan around in his snow-white capes. Rebecca Hall, playing his elegantly domineering wife, gets even less. Deep into the second act, Drew Starkey has an all-timer of an intro as elite operative Cyrus, the camera practically caressing his bare torso as he rolls on molly and ogles G-string-clad women in a sex club. But I’d be hard-pressed to say what the character actually accomplishes beyond stand around various scenes of carnage; at one point, in fact, he’s explicitly instructed not to do anything at all.

The political themes hinted at by the opening collage — clips of robot soldiers and photos of Abu Ghraib torture victims and headlines about the U.S. embrace of Nazi scientists after World War II, all conspiring to remind us that the American military has always been capable of profound horror — never completely fade from view. But they never really get fleshed out any further, either. The potential to tap into the ambient paranoia of our current militarized age goes unfulfilled.

What Onslaught does remember to develop are the good guys, far less colorful than the villains but, in their down-to-earth relatability, no less compelling. Celeste should be another feather in the cap for Arjona, a wonderfully versatile actor who’s been steadily on the rise for the past few years. Here, she gets to glower and shoot and make a bloody mess with the best of the action-hero badasses. But she also gets to demonstrate the humor and warmth that’s made her such a delight in films like Hit-Man.

She’s especially winsome in her scenes with Josiah, the two grizzled vets teasing each other or coming to each other’s aid with the unspoken kinship that comes from shared experience. It’s his unassuming decency, even more than Daisy’s sweet innocence or Celeste’s mama-bear toughness, that makes Windy Oasis feel like a world worth saving. One only wishes the film could have done the same while also making a fully satisfying meal of the cartoonish villains who’ve come to destroy them.

Friday AUGUST 28

 

The Modern Warfare 4 Open Beta arrives at 10 AM PT today. Thank you for sharing your experiences, best plays, and feedback with us during Weekend 1. Your input is helping shape the experience as we continue to make improvements.

 

We’ve made some sweeping changes to the game with focus on a few key areas: TTK, Spawns, Movement, Killstreaks and Aim Assist.

 

TIME-TO-KILL

After some updates last week, we still weren’t where we wanted to be with time-to-kill. We’re aiming for a slight increase to TTK so instead of changing base health, we focused on weapon tuning to improve durability without making weapons feel too weak at range. Every single weapon in our Beta has received an update for Weekend 2. These changes create more survivability and room for skill expression in combat.There’s more work to do here and we’re looking forward to hearing your feedback.

 

SPAWNS

In the final hours of Weekend 1, we adjusted spawns and spawn logic across all respawn modes to better separate players. Additionally, we greatly reduced spawning on squad members. 

 

For Weekend 2, we wanted to build on these changes with adjustments to Hardpoint specifically. We feel the mode plays best when spawns are consistent and predictable. The prototype in the Beta today is a step toward that vision, but it is far from perfect. You may still see some bad spawns on smaller maps, and on larger maps you may spawn too far from the action. We are excited about the direction and will be improving things with your feedback.

 

Finally, we added Battle Hardened to the temporary spawn protection, reducing the effects of flash and concussion grenades immediately after spawning.

 

  • Updated spawn logic to better separate players [added at the end of Beta Weekend 1]
  • Deprioritized spawning near teammates [added at the end of Beta Weekend 1]
  • Partially improved Hardpoint spawn system to improve predictability
  • Added Battle Hardened to temporary spawn protection
  • Temporarily disabled Hardpoint on Rooftops because of a spawn bug

We saw a lot of feedback about Tactical Sprint over Weekend 1, and we know there are a range of opinions about it. We have removed Tactical Sprint by default, which we think improves the pace of combat and gives the game a more classic feel. For players who prefer a faster playstyle, we moved it to a Perk and enhanced it by reducing its sprint-to-fire speed penalty. We have also adjusted Tac Sprint and slide speeds to rebalance them against each other.

 

This is an experiment for Beta which we hope improves the pace of the game and enhances player choice. If we decide to stick with this change, we need to consider its place in the Perk table and which other adjustments to Perks go along with it.

WELCOME TO THE RESURGENCE OPEN BETA

Our teams are locked-in for this weekend, and our first-ever Call of Duty: Warzone mode in a Beta! This preview covers some of the key details to know heading into a new Resurgence experience once Beta is live beginning tomorrow August 28th at 10 AM PT.

 

It’s been a great collaboration for us at Infinity Ward working with  Raven Software and Beenox, and the many other teams that are bringing this next chapter to life. Having Resurgence in Beta will provide an early look at what’s ahead for Warzone, giving our teams important feedback and gameplay insights

 

Let’s dive in.


INTRODUCING ZODIAC

Zodiac is the newest Resurgence map coming to Warzone. Located in South Korea within the broader setting of MW4, the map drops players into a weapons manufacturing facility where weapons are built and shipped around the world. The setting gives the map plenty of personality, with 10 unique and varied points of interest such as the Old Mine, Solar, Trackline, and the sewers. Together, they offer a mix of striking visuals, combat scenarios, different elevations, and plenty to explore.

Across the map, players will encounter moving solar panels, furnace conveyor belts, dynamic signage warning them about incoming trains, and intense fights across multiple levels, including sniper battles from the burning Admin Tower. Meanwhile, the incoming gas storm makes sure no one can stay comfortable for too long. Built by the team behind Rebirth Island and Vondel, Zodiac brings years of Warzone experience together with new mechanics, memorable moments, and plenty for players to discover.


THE PLAYLIST

Tomorrow, we’ll kick things off with Resurgence Quads, and will rotate in Casual Resurgence Quads across the duration of the Open Beta. As we focus on Beta, Resurgence Quads and Casual Resurgence Quads will be temporarily disabled in the live game. We want as many Resurgence players as possible to jump into Beta for the first time and share their feedback so we can make improvements ahead of launch later this year.


GAMEPLAY

The movement you’ll experience tomorrow in Resurgence will be closely aligned with MW4 Multiplayer. You’ll find that you’ll be able to navigate Zodiac in a more grounded and deliberate  way, without sacrificing the fluidity and momentum that larger maps in Warzone call for.

 

This Open Beta features MW4’s arsenal of weapons, with Default Loadouts and ground loot weapons hand-crafted by our team. While Custom Loadouts will not be available, we’ve ensured that tomorrow’s Default Loadouts offer a solid variety of weapon and equipment combinations. As for where things deviate from Multiplayer, we’ve tuned weapon damage ranges, bullet velocity, ADS speed, sprint-to-fire speed, and mobility to meet Warzone’s specific needs - with weapon time-to-kill designed to feel familiar to players coming from the live game.

 

We’re also introducing gameplay elements to Resurgence designed to create more emergent moments throughout a match. Fuel barrels will be the first taste of this, giving you a dynamic way to interact with the environment and another reason to pay attention to where you’re taking cover. 

 

Killstreaks will include a broader selection from Multiplayer,, with the most powerful ones remaining intentionally rare. You’ll also find new ways to defend yourself, like the SAM Turret Field Upgrade which lets you counter aerial threats.

 

Among other changes, Recon Contracts now reward a single-use Insight Killstreak, which will give you the freedom to choose when to activate your earned Circle Peek - providing a massive intel boost when timed correctly. You’ll notice that Supply Run Contracts have been updated to provide a one-time discount and an upgrade to Buy Stations with exclusive items.

 

As this is still a Beta build, some systems and features are not available in the Open Beta but are planned for launch later this year, including Daily Challenges, as well as some Killstreaks, Tactical Equipment, and Field Upgrades. We’ll share information about the full slate of these systems, along with any future content, as we get closer to launch.

On behalf of everyone across Infinity Ward and our partners, Ready Up! We've been waiting for this moment for a long time, and we're incredibly excited to finally share Modern Warfare 4 with all of you. 

This Beta is for the community. It's for the culture. It's your opportunity to jump in, put everything to the test, and help shape what's next for Modern Warfare.

We can't wait to see the moments you create, the stories you'll tell, and the feedback you'll share.

From all of us at Infinity Ward, thank you for believing in what Modern Warfare can be and for being part of this journey with us. Now it's your turn. Jump into the Beta, squad up with your friends, make some incredible memories, and show us what you've got.

The Modern Warfare 4 Beta is almost here. 

 

This page is your home base throughout the Beta. We’ll keep it updated with the latest patch notes, live issues, and updates from the team. If something changes, you’ll find it here.

 

Weekend One is your first chance to jump into Modern Warfare 4 Multiplayer and get hands-on with new movement, weapons, maps, modes, and systems we’ve been building for the past few years.

 

For the first time in a Call of Duty Beta, we’re also opening up a full Campaign mission, giving you an early look at the story, characters, and world of Modern Warfare 4 before launch.

 

And this is just the beginning. When the Open Beta returns for Weekend Two, we’ll raise the Player Level cap, unlock additional Multiplayer content, and bring Warzone Resurgence into the mix with our brand-new map, Zodiac.

 

The Beta is one of the most important parts of development. It’s our opportunity to put Modern Warfare 4 through its paces at scale, and your opportunity to help shape the experience. Throughout both weekends, we'll be watching, listening, and working behind the scenes to make each day better than the day before.

 

So jump in, put Modern Warfare 4 to the test, and let us know what you think. We can't wait to hear your feedback. 

It all kicks off tomorrow with Call of Duty NEXT. Tune-in tomorrow at 9:00 AM PT for a first look at the Modern Warfare 4 Beta. Our developers will be sharing new gameplay details, giving you a closer look at what’s coming, including Call of Duty: Warzone news.

Mobility Course 

MW4’s grounded movement prioritizes fluidity and freedom. We made a Mobility Course for players to learn, experiment, and master the system. Spend a few minutes learning the basics, or a few hours challenging yourself for the best time possible. Either way, you'll feel the difference the next time you load into Multiplayer.

 

Weapons

Weekend One gives you access to 14 weapons that showcase MW4’s variety, personality, and balance. The team has worked hard on handling, presentation, and gameplay with the goal of delivering the best first-person gunplay we’ve ever made. Gunsmith lets you push the boundaries of each weapon’s capabilities, and Apex Attachments let you take those builds even further.

 

With weapon progression, we cut down redundant attachment grinding. Attachments you've already earned can be used on other guns as well, giving you more customization options faster as your arsenal expands.

 

We’ve spent countless hours playtesting these weapons, honing their designs, and dialing in the tuning, and we’re excited to finally get them into the hands of our players.

 

Here’s are some Apex Attachments the team suggests you try out in Beta:

  • The Han 86 transforms into the Han X20 Skybreaker. This advanced weapons system mounts to the top of the receiver and allows the platform to deploy 20mm airburst rounds which detonate at a specified distance.
  • The X-58 Nyx becomes the X-58 Void. Complete with a brass catcher and an extended, wrapped suppressor, the X-58 Void is the ultimate stealth platform - hiding enemy death markers and obfuscating the directional hit indicators of its targets.

 

Killstreaks 

In MW4's Killstreak system, a kill still counts as a point no matter what mode you're in. However, we want to make sure we reward objective players as well. With our new Smart Streak layer, taking a Domination Flag, holding a Hardpoint, or planting the Data Spike all contribute to your Killstreak Meter. 

 

Progression & Rewards 

Every Multiplayer match earns XP toward your Player Level, unlocking additional gameplay content as you progress through Beta.

 

During Weekend One, the level cap is Level 20. When the Open Beta begins in Weekend Two, the cap increases to Level 30, with additional Weapons, Equipment, Perks, Killstreaks, and rewards.

PC Experience 

 

For more on the Beta experience on PC, check out the COD Blog.

 

As a reminder, PC players must have TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot enabled to play the Modern Warfare 4 Beta online.

 

These Windows security features provide a trusted foundation for RICOCHET Anti-Cheat and make system-level tampering more difficult, helping protect the integrity of the Beta from Day One.

 

If you already have TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot enabled, you’re ready to go. If either feature is disabled, you won’t be able to play the Beta online.

 

Players can also run the Call of Duty Secure Attestation Wizard before jumping in to verify their PC meets the required security standards.

 

Feedback and Live Issues 

The Beta is a critically important part of testing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 at scale. Expect daily updates for bug fixes, gameplay adjustments, and new maps and modes.

 

Below is a list of known issues that we’re currently investigating:

  • 4x optics may display incorrectly while aiming down sights 
  • The loadout selection screen may remain visible after a match begins 
  • When observing other players transition from slide to sprint, there may be animation timing discrepancies 
  • Joining a party may lead to a "Press A to Start" or black screen when accessing the Quick Nav 
  • Quick Draw attachments may cause a frame rate drop in ADS 
  • PC Players may experience a hitch in their first match played
  • Use of recording software such as NVIDIA ShadowPlay may cause hitching on some PCs 

 

You can track the status of known issues and get the latest updates from the team on the official Modern Warfare 4 Trello Board.  

 

If something seems broken to you… it probably is. Share it with us so we can help. Please include your platform, match ID (in the bottom left-hand corner of your screen), and any photos or videos to help us fix things faster. 

 

In addition to the Modern Warfare 4 Patch Notes, you can find additional real-time communications from us through @CODUpdates on X and @InfinityWard across platforms.

 

We’ll be right here playing this game with you, listening to the conversation, and digging into feedback during Beta. 

 

Ready up. We’ll see you online.

Liverpool sign Barcola from PSG in potential £123m deal

Liverpool have completed the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain for an initial £106m fee, which could rise to £123m. The France international has signed a five-year deal at Anfield. Andoni Iraola has prioritised signing wingers this summer after replacing Arne Slot. Barcola follows the arrival of Victor Muñoz as the former Bournemouth head coach aims to rebuild the frontline.

The 23-year-old was a long-term target for Liverpool who have tracked his progress over a number of seasons. Completing the transfer has been delayed while PSG awaited making their own signings to compensate for Barcola’s exit. The winger attracted interested from other clubs but as adamant that he was only willing to join Liverpool and has ignored other offers.

Liverpool have targeted younger players in this window, evidenced by the signings of 21-year-old Jérémy Jacquet and 23-year-old Muñoz in the hope of building a squad for the long-term.

Tottenham news now, and it looks like Kevin Danso is off to Sunderland and Spurs are reportedly targeting Tosin Adarabioyo as his centre-back replacement – yet another new signing for Roberto De Zerbi’s men. Tosin looks to be well down the pecking order at Chelsea, if not a confirmed ‘bomb squad’ member this summer.

Also, the BBC have gazumped my £100m player quiz by naming them all in their live blog – don’t look now!

A (welcome) change of pace here from the high-octane, high-calibre transfer stuff. Nicky Bandini takes a look at Fiorentina’s fortunes in Serie A.

A slight correction from earlier: the Barcola deal will not quite be a British transfer record even if the add-ons are achieved to take it from £106m to £123m. That honour still belongs to the Alexander Isak to Liverpool deal, which was worth £125m.

There have now been nine signings by Premier League clubs that have surpassed the £100m mark.

Can you name the other seven not named in this post? Three were for Chelsea, two for Manchester City, one for Arsenal and one other for Liverpool.

So in lieu of a left-back or another centre-forward, could Manchester United’s best signing be tying Fernandes down for another few years? He is so important to that team.

Not that United’s army of online fans are likely to be placated if the club fail to land another genuine signing before the deadline.

Manchester United open contract talks with Fernandes

Manchester United have opened initial discussions with Bruno Fernandes regarding a new deal, with the captain currently earning in the region of £220,00 a-week.

The club hold a one-year option to extent the 31-year-old’s current contract, which expires next summer but are intent on him agreeing to sign on again for the longer term.

Last season, Fernandes’ stellar form won him both major footballer of the year awards and he has continued in similar mode this year, scoring a hat-trick in Sunday’s 5-2 trouncing of Ipswich at Old Trafford. Fernandes will be 32 on 8 September.

Some Barcola reaction for you, including a pronunciation guide for Manchester City fans:

Kev McCready says: “As an LFC fan, Barcola will improve us tremendously. I’ll miss Gakpo, having only just learned how to pronounce his name correctly. It’s been a strange window, with some gaps still remaining and possibly two young players coming in next year (Bruggmans, N’Guessan). Don’t want to appear ungrateful, but a six and a two would have been nice. It’s HACK-po by the way, City fans.”

Krishna: “Regarding Barcola, we once signed one Fernando Torres for a then record transfer fee of £50m and Barry Glendenning later called him a fish for his aversion to find the net.”

Chelsea target Koné as Fernandez replacement

Chelsea are interested in Roma’s Manu Koné as a possible replacement for Enzo Fernández, who remains likely to join Manchester City before the transfer window shuts.

However, the France midfielder is one of several names on Chelsea’s shortlist. They also like Monaco’s Lamine Camara and their interest in Bournemouth’s Alex Scott and Crystal Palace’s Adam Wharton is no secret. A possible move for Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White has been played down to me.

Chelsea say they need to improve their squad if they are to sell Fernández. That could mean them signing both a winger and a midfielder.

Barcola has been chatting to the Liverpool website about making the move to Merseyside from Paris – and he’s aiming big:

“It took a long time but I’m really happy today to be able to play for Liverpool,” he said. “I hope to achieve very big things. First of all, winning the Premier League – it’s one of my biggest dreams in my life.

“It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term – that’s why I signed a long contract – and I hope I can do it.”

Thanks Gregg.

Doesn’t it feel strange that a Premier League club can pay £123m for a player – a British transfer record – and we can all just collectively shrug? Make no mistake, Barcola is a fine footballer though, it will be fascinating to see how he fares at Anfield.

Now that I’ve helped Liverpool get the Barcola signing over the line, I’ll hand back over to Dom. Bye!

Liverpool sign Barcola from PSG in potential £123m deal

Liverpool have completed the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain for an initial £106m fee, which could rise to £123m. The France international has signed a five-year deal at Anfield. Andoni Iraola has prioritised signing wingers this summer after replacing Arne Slot. Barcola follows the arrival of Victor Muñoz as the former Bournemouth head coach aims to rebuild the frontline.

The 23-year-old was a long-term target for Liverpool who have tracked his progress over a number of seasons. Completing the transfer has been delayed while PSG awaited making their own signings to compensate for Barcola’s exit. The winger attracted interested from other clubs but as adamant that he was only willing to join Liverpool and has ignored other offers.

Liverpool have targeted younger players in this window, evidenced by the signings of 21-year-old Jérémy Jacquet and 23-year-old Muñoz in the hope of building a squad for the long-term.

We have an email from someone who has watched Jamie Jaleel Jeremy Leweling (yep, that’s a great name) far more than I have. “I’ve been a fan of Jamie Leweling since he signed for Stuttgart, so I’m thrilled at the idea of him joining Liverpool,” writes Morgan Blake. “If it had been up to me, Liverpool would have gone in for him last summer. Terrific player.” Bild are now reporting that Roma have now submitted second bid of €35m for the winger, however.

Allan has been talking on the Manchester City website about how proud he is to be joining the 10-times champions.

This is a surreal moment for me. Manchester City, with everything they have won over the past 15 years, are one of the most attractive clubs in the world for players. To be able to sit here today and say I have joined them is the proudest moment of my life. I love Palmeiras and always will – but the decision to come to City was an easy one. I want to be the best footballer I can be and the conversations I’ve had with the people at City so far has convinced me there isn’t a better place for me to fulfil my ambitions. I want to promise the Manchester City fans I will give absolutely everything to make the most of this opportunity. Now the hard work begins. I will give 100% in training and make the best case possible to the manager I should be playing. My intention is to help City continue winning trophies. Doku, Semenyo, Monga, Cherki, Foden and possibly Gakpo. He’ll have a fair bit of competition from forwards/wingers at the Etihad. He is versatile, though. Good luck to the lad.

Wingers are so “in” right now and Sky Sport Germany are reporting that Liverpool and Everton are going to battle it out for Stuttgart wide man Jamie Leweling. The 25-year-old Germany international is reportedly also of interest to Roma. Everton have their hands full sorting ins and outs over the next 24 hours, with the Toffees looking to offload Beto and potentially bring back Jack Grealish and Richarlison to the club, as well as finalising a deal for Folarin Balogun. That would be good news for Everton-supporting Andy Burnham – the UK prime minister would then have an easy ice-breaker if he stumbles into Donald Trump at the UN general assembly.

Claudio Echeverri is expected to be loaned to Benfica by Manchester City for the season. The 20-year-old forward joined in January 2024 from River Plate. The Argentinian has made three City appearances and previously had temporary spells at Bayer Leverkusen and Girona, one of City’s sister clubs.

It’s made the length of contracts seem more important than ever. It’s little wonder some players are forever scrawling their signatures on longer deals.

Sunderland are interested in a deal for the Lyon winger Malick Fofana. The 21-year-old Belgian has two goals in six games this season.

Thanks Dom. Hello folks. Let’s get this lunchtime stint started then, eh? And what better way than to focus on a club that has seemingly taken up most of the transfer window’s bandwidth this summer, Tottenham Hotspur! It’s not a big slice of news, to be honest, with talented teenage forward Mikey Moore heading to Köln on loan. There’s no deal in place for a potential sale, which shows that Spurs still value the player and expect him back, perhaps with a little more polish, next summer. And while we’re on the subject of the Bundesliga, read all about Elversberg’s big win at the weekend. They’re the German top flight’s village people, in case you were wondering.

Manchester City sign Allan in £34m deal

Manchester City have confirmed the signing of Allan Elias from Palmeiras in a €37.5m plus €2.5m (£34m) deal. The 22-year-old wide forward made his senior debut for Palmeiras last year and has made 96 appearances for the club, scoring nine goals and making 12 assists. Allan is City’s third major acquisition of the window following Elliot Anderson, for £116m, and Ayyoub Bouaddi, for £85m. City are open to a loan for Jack Grealish, with Everton hopeful of taking the 30-year-old.

And on that bombshell, I shall hand over to Gregg Bakowski for the next hour. Plenty more transfer news to come!

Muñoz signs for Forest in £22m transfer from Palace

Nottingham Forest have added a key component: Daniel Muñoz has reunited with Oliver Glasner after signing in a £22m deal from Crystal Palace. One of Glasner’s priorities this window was a right-wing back.

The 30-year-old Colombia international, part of Palace’s Conference League and FA Cup triumphs under Glasner, has signed a three-year contract, with the option of a further 12 months. Muñoz could make his Forest debut at home to Tottenham on Saturday.

Burnley defender Joe Worrall is closing in on a move to Championship rivals Wrexham after the clubs agreed a fee in the region for £2m.

The centre-back has never become a regular at Turf Moor and is expected to sign a three-year deal with at the Racecourse Ground.

Burnley could move for a centre-back to replace him, and have previously been interested in Galatasaray’s Victor Nelsson, who is available for free.

Hull and Ipswich may already have Premier League wins under their belts, but the two promoted teams are not done when it comes to incoming transfers. And it seems they are targeting the best Championship talent, a pretty standard move for newly-promoted sides.

Sky are reporting that Hull have agreed a deal to sign Sorba Thomas from Stoke – but that the Potters want to find a replacement before sanctioning the winger’s exit – while Ipswich, according to TeamTalk, are closing in on Burnley striker Zian Flemming.

If it wasn’t already clear at times last season, it should be from the start of this. He’s far from the player he was even in Liverpool’s recent title-winning year and is often the source of their defensive problems now (with lack of pace and subsequent poor positioning) rather than the solution to them.

Chelsea: It’s genuinely hard to keep track of Chelsea’s ever-changing squad and it should be of no surprise to anyone that the Blues look likely to conduct more business before tomorrow’s deadline.

Xabi Alonso’s side may have to accommodate for the departure of Enzo Fernández, who could join Manchester City, so have Lamine Camara – also linked with Liverpool – and Roma’s French midfielder Manu Koné on their shortlist of replacements. Chelsea have already signed Valentín Barco and Jordan Henderson to boost their midfield numbers this summer, with Moises Caicedo and Roméo Lavia among Alonso’s first choices.

It’s another Rubik’s Cube of transfer possibilities Chelsea will have to unscramble in the next day or so.

Harry Maguire waxed lyrical about Mainoo after the 21-year-old all-round stellar midfield display at Old Trafford on Sunday.

“That’s probably credit to Michael and his staff. But I think without the ball now, he’s becoming a real monster in there, and he wins a lot of second balls. He wins a lot of duels. “He’s so young, if we want him to play for this club for another 10 years, there’s going to be times where he’s going to go through a patch like with Rashy and myself, but that’s part and parcel. Liverpool: Why do the Reds want to sell Cody Gakpo, I hear you ask?

It’s a good question as Gakpo, despite some criticism from fans at times, has been pretty consistent during his three-and-a-half years at Anfield, scoring 51 goals in around 180 appearances for Liverpool, playing almost exclusively on the left wing.

The departure of Mohamed Salah, plus the signing of Victor Muñoz, the emergence of Rio Ngumoha and the pending arrival of Bradley Barcola have all contributed to a situation where Liverpool believe selling Gakpo and reinvesting the cash would be a wise move.

Ngumoha, Muñoz and Barcola are all better on the left flank, where Gakpo likes to play, while Liverpool have right-sided forwards – such as Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh and Ismaïla Sarr of Crystal Palace – on their radar. It seems Liverpool want to address the balance of their attack and Gakpo is the fall guy. Still, selling to Manchester City, as has been suggested, would be surprising. Big clubs don’t like to sell first team players to their rivals.

The Rumour Mill is the only place to start, if you will forgive the self-promotion, given I was tasked with writing today’s edition.

A merry-go-round of wide forwards could be upon us in the final days of the window.

Preamble

The end of a long summer of transfers is nigh: but not before a final, desperate, scrap for signings ensues in the final couple of days of the window. It never ceases to amaze us how and why clubs allow this to happen… but it provides compelling reading and watching as the deals roll in.

There are a number of ‘sagas’ to keep your eyes on: Cody Gakpo, Enzo Fernández and Ismaïla Sarr are three high-profile Premier League stars who could be on the move, with Liverpool, Chelsea and Manchester City three big clubs who ought to be very active in the next day or two. They won’t be alone. The signings keep on coming at Tottenham – and the Spurs owners may decree that more are required after a disappointing start to the season. Then there is Manchester United and their left-back situation, while lower down the English top flight the likes of Fulham and Crystal Palace, with new managers, will feel they must strengthen. And don’t forget about big deals around the continent, and in the women’s game.

So much to happen, to little time. Do join us throughout today and tomorrow as we build towards that 11pm (BST) transfer deadline tomorrow (Tuesday) when the window – and we’re obliged to say this – SLAMS SHUT. The deadline for WSL clubs is on Thursday 3 September.

NEW YORK (AP) — The Metropolitan Museum of Art is canceling its planned exhibit honoring British designer John Galliano, which had led to severe backlash in the Jewish community and beyond because of the designer’s past antisemitic and racist statements.

The museum said Monday that the exhibit, which had been planned as the May 2027 spring Costume Institute show launching the annual Met Gala, will be replaced by another show to be announced later.

“Following thoughtful discussions with John Galliano, we have together decided not to proceed with the exhibition,” Max Hollein, director and CEO of the museum, announced in a statement.

The designer joined in the statement, saying: “After much reflection and discussion with The Met and all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time. I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry for it.”

Galliano, long recognized as one of the fashion world’s biggest talents for his flamboyant designs, was at the pinnacle of that world for years as creative director of Christian Dior. He was fired from the post when a series of racist and antisemitic comments from 2010 and 2011 surfaced and went viral, leading to his conviction in an antisemitism trial in France.

Dropped by Dior, Galliano spent several years involved in public and private efforts to rehabilitate. He made a comeback in 2014 when he was hired by Paris fashion house Maison Margiela, where he remained for a decade.

He was to become only the third living designer to be the subject of a solo show at the Met’s Costume Institute.

The spring is launched by the annual Met Gala, the most visible event on the fashion calendar. The gala is overseen by Anna Wintour, Vogue’s global editorial director and one of the most influential figures in global fashion. Wintour has been a longtime friend and supporter of Galliano.

The museum had held discussions with Jewish community leaders before announcing the show, hoping to ward off anticipated backlash. But the anger only increased. One of the key critics of the planned show was New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin, who issued a statement Monday praising the decision to cancel.

“After my numerous and lengthy meetings and conversations with The Met, I am pleased that they have agreed to not honor John Galliano,” Menin said. “From the beginning, I have told them that I strongly disagreed with this decision, and at this rising time of antisemitism, it had served as a gut punch to the Jewish community. This is the correct decision, as the harm and pain this was causing was simply unacceptable.”

articles.title: Police to Send Case Against HYBE Chairman Bang Si-hyuk to Prosecutors
articles.excerpt: Police will refer HYBE Chairman Bang Si-hyuk to prosecutors over alleged 190 billion won in improper IPO gains, the National Office of Investigation said.
articles.content:
Referral on Bang expected within this week Case involving independent lawmaker Kim Byung-kee "Nearing completion, referral to come soon"

Hong Seok-ki, head of the National Office of Investigation at the Korean National Police Agency, told a press briefing at the agency's headquarters in Seodaemun-gu, Seoul, on Oct. 31 that he had "been briefed that the case is right before referral." On whether Bang would be detained, Hong said, "We plan to refer the case this week, and the decision on custody will come at that time."

Bang is suspected of telling investors in 2019 that Hybe had no IPO plans, inducing them to sell their stakes to a particular private equity fund. That fund sold large blocks of shares after Hybe's 2022 listing. Police believe Bang improperly pocketed 190 billion won, or 30% of the sale proceeds, under an undisclosed contract with the fund. They also concluded that Bang was involved in setting up and operating the fund, which was capitalized by Hybe executives.

Police said they would also soon conclude the case involving Kim. "I've been briefed that it will wrap up soon," Hong said. "There appears to have been a wait because a request for an investigation review committee was filed during the process. I understand it will come out shortly."

Hong denied suggestions that police were deliberately delaying the investigation until the launch of the new prosecution service. "Considering that the review committee resolved to conclude the case within a month, you can expect it to be referred very soon," he said.

Asked about a former aide who exposed various allegations of misconduct by Kim and has petitioned the National Police Commission to launch inspections of current and former heads of the National Office of Investigation, Hong said, "From the investigative agency's standpoint, there were 13 items under investigation, and unlike how it looks from the outside, there was a great deal to substantiate." He added, "That is what stretched out the timeline. Of course, from the perspective of those who filed the complaints, it has been more than 11 months, so I think they can file a grievance."

A’ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum will miss the FIBA Women’s World Cup for health reasons and will be replaced by Washington teammates Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron, USA Basketball announced Monday.

Wilson, the four-time WNBA MVP, has shouldered quite a workload in the first part of the season for the Las Vegas Aces and needed a break to rest and get ready for the playoffs. She was voted the most outstanding player of the 2024 Paris Olympics and the 2022 World Cup. She will be sorely missed by the United States.

Plum has been dealing with a calf injury for most of the WNBA season and it still hasn’t 100% healed. She was a catalyst in the Paris Games gold-medal contest against France and sparked the Americans to the one-point victory.

Iriafen and Citron were both part of U.S. camps this past winter. Iriafen played on the American team that went to Puerto Rico and won the World Cup qualifier. Citron had to miss that tournament because of an injury, so she’ll be making her national team debut in Germany.

The Americans have won every World Cup since finishing with the bronze medal in 2006. That World Cup saw American star Lisa Leslie pull out at the last minute because of a car accident that her uncle was in. Without her, the U.S. fell to Russia in the semifinals.

Without the two veteran players, the U.S. will rely even more heavily on its youth movement. Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers will make their World Cup debut. The young stars will be joined by Olympic medalists Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier, Chelsea Gray, Jackie Young and Kahleah Copper.

Rhyne Howard and Aliyah Boston will also be making their World Cup debuts to round out the team.

The U.S. opens against China on Friday. The Chinese team has a huge front line with 7-foot-3 Zhang Ziyu, 6-10 Han Xu and 6-7 Li Yueru. The two teams played for the World Cup title in 2022 in Australia.

articles.title: Edouard dumps over 20 inches of rain on Texas, and the flood threat isn’t over | CNN
articles.excerpt: Heavy rain from former Tropical Storm Edouard is still falling on eastern Texas, but relief is coming.
articles.content:
Heavy rain from former Tropical Storm Edouard is still falling on eastern Texas nearly two days after the storm made landfall, but relief is coming.

🌧️ In the storm’s path? Track it, get local insights from meteorologists and more, only in the CNN Weather app ⛈️

The flood threat should finally ease Thursday afternoon, but flash flood warnings were in effect Thursday morning for a batch of slow-moving downpours near Palestine and Lufkin, Texas.

The ongoing flood risk is 50 to 100 miles northwest of areas hardest hit Wednesday. A month’s worth of rain fell in an hour and localized rainfall totals topped 20 inches in the area north of Beaumont, Texas, resulting in dangerous flash flooding and water rescues.

Another round of torrential rain Wednesday night dumped 2 to 4 inches per hour on some of the same saturated locations.

Heavy rain should lose its steam on Thursday afternoon. Hit-or-miss storms are possible through Friday, but the overall flood danger is much lower.

River flooding could linger long after the heaviest rain ends. River flood warnings are in effect along the Neches River and several tributaries, with some extending into the weekend.

Edouard’s legacy

Tiny Tropical Storm Edouard pelted the Texas-Louisiana border region with strong winds as it intensified through landfall on Tuesday, but extreme rainfall will be its legacy.

It started when the storm got stuck over the same areas of eastern Texas Tuesday night through Wednesday, wringing out 10 to 21 inches of rain. A flash flood emergency — the highest level of flood warning from the National Weather Service — was issued on Wednesday morning in parts of Hardin and Tyler counties as a result.

Roughly a dozen motorists were rescued after driving into water on roadways in Hardin County, according to a county emergency management news release. Two people were also rescued from a home that had flooded. Around 10 structures were damaged by fallen trees and limbs, and one commercial building sustained “extensive roof damage,” according to the release.

An assisted living facility in the county was also damaged, requiring responders to evacuate 21 people who are unable to walk on their own, according to the Texas Game Wardens, whose personnel assisted.

The flash flood emergency expired late Wednesday morning, but a new one was issued Wednesday night for Saratoga and nearby parts of western Hardin County, which received more than 6 inches of rain in about two hours.

Highway 787 was closed because of high water, and several water rescues were conducted Wednesday night, according to the National Weather Service. CNN has reached out to local authorities for additional details.

To the northeast, in neighboring Polk County, authorities helped five people leave a mobile home surrounded by water, County Judge Sydney Murphy told CNN. The five included three children and a baby, CNN affiliate KPRC reported. Floodwater was around waist-deep in the area after a nearby creek overflowed.

Murphy issued a local disaster declaration Wednesday due to Edouard’s impacts.

The storm’s winds, which gusted from 60 to 90 mph near the Texas-Louisiana border, downed trees and limbs and power lines across multiple Texas counties. Power is still out for more than 30,000 homes and businesses across eastern Texas as of early Thursday morning, according to PowerOutage.com.

El Niño is bossing hurricane season

Another short-lived storm fits with what the 2026 Atlantic season has delivered so far due to a strengthening and potentially record-breaking El Niño.

The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season’s activity is running just 11% of average as of September 1, according to one measure .

Dolly fell apart in the open Atlantic on August 28 after just 24 hours. Cristobal disintegrated just as quickly in the northern Atlantic on August 13. The other two storms, Arthur and Bertha, had brief shelf lives in the Gulf in June and July, respectively.

The Atlantic basin is now set to experience its latest first hurricane since 2013, according to satellite-assisted records dating to 1966. The record latest first hurricane is September 11, set by Gustav in 2002 and tied by Humberto in 2013.

September is the typical peak of Atlantic hurricane season thanks to a combination of more favorable weather ingredients.

The most basic building block is warmer water temperatures, which peak in September after basking in summer’s heat, and provide fuel for storms to form and strengthen.

Lower wind shear, aka tropical-system kryptonite, is the other big ingredient. Wind shear involves changes in wind speed and direction at different levels of the atmosphere, and it can rip apart anything from budding tropical systems to fully developed hurricanes.

But this year’s El Niño has made wind shear unusually strong and widespread in the tropical Atlantic and Caribbean. That has stifled storm chances and ripped apart storms like Dolly.

It’s also the main reason forecasters have called for a muted season overall.

But that’s no reason to ignore the rest of hurricane season completely. Storms can still find windows of opportunity to form and become a threat, even in an overall subdued season.

CNN Meteorologists Dakota Smith, Tyler Ory and Mary Gilbert contributed to this report.

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 beta Steam numbers haven't budged in the second weekend, despite Warzone's arrival and transformative patch
articles.excerpt: Although many would argue the second beta weekend of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 was better in key ways, the numbers seemingly didn't reflect that.
articles.content:
UAVoidable.

We're deep in the second and final session of the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 beta. This open portion is available on one more platform - Switch 2, and can be accessed without the need for a pre-order. It also includes a sampler of Warzone's next Resurgence map and two Ground War maps, alongside all the maps and modes from the first beta weekend. None of that appears to have moved the needle, at least on Steam.

The beta's peak concurrent player count of 115,145, which was achieved over the first weekend, has yet to be beaten. The closest it has got was a little over 113,000 on Friday, likely due to player interest in Warzone. Of course, it's always worth keeping in mind that we have no visibility on PlayStation 5, Xbox or Switch 2 numbers - it's possible some or all of those platforms saw big turnouts in the second weekend.

All that said, Steam is often a good barometer for the performance of most major games, and it's notable that despite the new stuff and the beta's free accessibility, the numbers didn't improve.

Beyond simply comparing and contrasting numbers, there's also the matter of the key gameplay changes Infinity Ward introduced to the beta this session to address the most popular points of feedback.

Once players got their hands on the game during the first weekend, it became clear that movement was going to be the first point of contention. Many believe the game's movement speed and movement abilities make for an uncontrollable pace, so Infinity Ward wanted to change several of those parameters to see if they'll make a difference. Even for a beta, this is unusual, especially considering the extent to which the developer was willing to go to address feedback.

For starters - as an experiment - the developer removed Tactical Sprint by default, tying it instead to the Blood Rush Perk. Tactical Sprint offers faster sprint speeds but delays how quickly you can get your gun up. Despite that penalty, players figured out years ago you can eliminate that by sliding out of it, essentially giving you two advantages. This was on display all across the first weekend, hence the change. Slides were also nerfed, with their distance and speed cut, and the slide-to-jump delay increased.

Time to Kill was another hotly-debated topic in weekend one because of how fast it felt. Infinity Ward addressed that by reducing the damage of every gun in the beta. Together with the movement changes, the pace of the game has slowed, and the time it takes to kill an opponent has increased alongside it.

The transformative patch tweaked spawns, too, to cut down on the chaos of the first weekend, where players were spawning at random points across the map next to teammates, rather than in more predictable spots at the edges of the map. The patch also made Killstreaks harder to get by increasing the required number of kills by one across the board to prevent spam.

As a result of all that, the beta's second weekend feels considerably different to play than the first. But whether or not you agree with the changes, I feel they offer enough incentive for both disgruntled players and those happy with the game's previous state to see the differences for themselves. At least on Steam, that clearly hasn't borne out by the numbers.
